hook: How does BFS explore an entire graph without ever getting lost?

narration.text: Breadth-first search explores a graph one layer at a time, visiting every neighbor before going deeper.
We start at A and enqueue its neighbors B and C. Then we dequeue B — its only new neighbor is D, so D joins the queue too.
Next we dequeue C, discovering E. Then D, whose neighbors are already queued — nothing new here.
Finally E leads us to F, and once F is dequeued with no new neighbors, every node has been visited.
Six nodes, five edges, one pass — breadth-first search reaches every reachable node in the fewest possible layers.
